errors.unclosedRef: Unclosed metric reference at position {position} — write it as [metric_name].
errors.notMetricName: "[{ref}]" is not a metric name — use the metric's machine name (letters, digits, _), e.g. [revenue].
errors.unexpectedChar: Unexpected "{char}" at position {position} — a formula is [metric] references, numbers, + - * / and parentheses.
errors.empty: The formula is empty — reference at least one metric, e.g. ([revenue] - [cost]) / [orders].
errors.endsUnexpectedly: The formula ends unexpectedly — a value or [metric] is missing.
errors.unclosedParen: A "(" is never closed — add the matching ")".
errors.unexpectedOp: Unexpected "{op}" — a value or [metric] was expected there.
errors.trailing: Unexpected {what} after the end of the formula — check for a missing operator.
errors.noRef: The formula references no metric — a composite metric must use at least one [metric].
errors.unknownRef: The formula references [{ref}], but this dataset has no such metric (available: {hasAvailable, select, yes {{available}} other {none yet}}). Define it first.
errors.notBasic: [{ref}] is itself a formula/ratio — a composite metric may only reference BASIC metrics (sum, count, avg, …), so reference its parts instead.
